title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten distinct UMBC places for studying, making, gathering, movement, and campus culture, supported by direct university sources.

cards.title: The Commons
cards.subtitle: UMBC student union, central campus
cards.notes: Use the student union as a practical between-class meeting point: its listed spaces include lounges, student organization areas, dining, and a game room.
cards.short_summary: A central building for meetings, services, meals, and campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC describes The Commons as its student union and says it hosts social, cultural, and recreational activities before, between, and after classes.
cards.access_notes: Check the Commons site for current building and department hours.

cards.title: The Commons Terrace
cards.subtitle: Outdoor terrace at The Commons
cards.notes: Bring a conversation or a packed meal outdoors when conditions allow; UMBC identifies the terrace as a lunch meeting spot and event venue.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Commons gathering area used for meals and programmed events.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC says the Commons Terrace is a regular meeting spot for lunch and hosts concerts, ice cream socials, and campus festivals.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor use is weather-dependent; consult event listings for programmed activities.

cards.title: The Quad
cards.subtitle: Lawn outside The Commons
cards.notes: Use the open lawn as a simple rendezvous point before a Commons event, or pause there on a walk between the library and student-union spaces.
cards.short_summary: A central campus green immediately associated with The Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC’s welcome guide lists The Quad among the outdoor resources at The Commons, and its destinations page identifies Quadmania as an all-campus spring festival.
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor space; follow posted event setups and campus policies.

cards.title: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.subtitle: 1000 Hilltop Circle
cards.notes: Start here when your group needs a shared academic base: the building combines broad collections with designated study areas and library services.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s main library building and a prominent campus study destination.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC calls the Albin O. Kuhn Library the visual centerpiece of campus and identifies it as open to the general public.
cards.access_notes: Building access and borrowing privileges differ; check the library’s current hours and visitor guidance.

cards.title: Albin O. Kuhn Library Gallery
cards.subtitle: First floor, Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Pair a library stop with the current exhibition: look for interpretive displays from UMBC collections and check gallery information before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor exhibition space within UMBC’s library building.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC states that Library Gallery exhibitions showcase photography, rare books, and other materials from the library’s collections.
cards.access_notes: Gallery is listed in Library room 105; verify current exhibition and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Retriever Learning Center
cards.subtitle: Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Choose this library space for a collaborative session: arrange the mobile furniture, use whiteboards or monitors, and leave quiet-floor work for later.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour collaborative library environment with flexible furnishings.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC Library describes the Retriever Learning Center as a 24-hour space for group study, discussion, collaboration, and academic coaching.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces, Lockers & Specialty Rooms – UMBC Library
cards.access_notes: The library lists the RLC as 24 hours; access may require UMBC credentials or vary during closures.

cards.title: Digital Media Lab
cards.subtitle: Room 216H, Albin O. Kuhn Library & Gallery
cards.notes: Reserve recording space or use the editing workstations when a class project needs audio, video, or graphic-design production rather than a standard desk.
cards.short_summary: A library media-creation lab with editing tools and recording spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Media Lab provides UMBC students, faculty, and staff with tools to create and edit audio, video, and graphic-design objects.
cards.access_notes: Available to UMBC community members; book recording rooms and review current equipment and hours information.

cards.entity_name: Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture
cards.title: Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Building, 105
cards.notes: Check whether an exhibition is on view, then make this a focused art stop with a friend or a change of scene from library study.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s Fine Arts Building exhibition and public-programming venue.
cards.evidence_claim: CADVC lists its location in the Fine Arts Building and states that its public hours apply when exhibitions are on view and the university is open.
cards.source_title: Visit Us – Center for Art, Design and Visual Culture
cards.access_notes: Currently exhibition-dependent; confirm the gallery’s status and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Retriever Activities Center
cards.subtitle: 1000 Hilltop Circle
cards.notes: Meet up for a walk on the indoor track, a scheduled class, or a workout; check facility rules and the current recreation schedule first.
cards.short_summary: UMBC’s recreation facility for fitness, aquatics, courts, and an indoor track.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC lists the RAC’s fitness studio, weight room, cardio balcony, arena track, and aquatics center among its facilities.
cards.access_notes: Current RAC hours are Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–8 p.m. and weekends noon–6 p.m.; hours and eligibility may change.

cards.title: Conservation and Environmental Research Areas
cards.subtitle: CERA trails near UMBC’s Research Park
cards.notes: Take the marked interpretive route from the Herbert Run Greenway entrance, stay on established paths, and use the CERA map to orient your walk.
cards.short_summary: A mapped campus-adjacent wooded research and trail area.
cards.evidence_claim: UMBC provides directions to CERA and identifies the Herbert Run Greenway and CERA Interpretive Trail by their marked blazes.
cards.source_title: Visit CERA – UMBC Department of Geography & Environmental Systems
cards.access_notes: Use the department’s route and trail map; remain on marked paths and plan for daylight and weather.
